content: Before using this medication, inform your doctor, midwife, or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could trigger allergic reactions or other complications. During pregnancy, this medication should only be used when absolutely necessary. It is not known whether this drug passes into breast milk. Drug interactions can alter the effectiveness of your medications or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Maintain a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs as well as herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. If someone has overdosed on this medication and is experiencing severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Do not dispose of medications by flushing them down the toilet or pouring them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This medication is used to prepare the cervix (the lower opening of the womb) for labor and delivery. It is typically used in women who are having a normal pregnancy and are at or near their delivery due date. Dinoprostone is a natural substance produced by the body in preparation for labor. This drug is inserted high into the vagina, next to the cervix, by a healthcare professional. You will be lying down during the placement of the medication and will usually need to remain lying down for two hours afterward. This medication should only be used in a hospital setting where trained medical care is available. You will be monitored for changes in your cervix, signs of active labor (such as water breaking or strong, sustained contractions), and the condition of your baby. The healthcare professional will remove the insert if side effects occur, after 12 hours, or when it is no longer needed. Side effects such as fever, nausea, vomiting, diarrhea, or abdominal pain are uncommon and usually mild. Remember that this medication has been prescribed because your doctor has determined that the benefits to you outweigh the risks of side effects. Rarely, this drug has caused injury to the womb (uterine rupture), which may require emergency surgery. Symptoms of uterine rupture include severe pain in the womb and an abnormal heart rate in the baby. A very serious allergic reaction to this drug is rare. This is not a complete list of possible side effects. In the U.S., contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
